is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus and Anopheles coluzzii (Abstract, Page 1; Table 1, Page 5).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes GSTe2 L119F and Rdl A296S (Abstract, Page 1; Page 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts and frequencies are provided for 92 mosquitoes: for GSTe2 L119F, 84/92 were RR and 8/92 were RS; for Rdl A296S, 91/92 were SS and 1/92 was RS (Page 7).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the rural locality of Kpome in southern Benin (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original collection and genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to the locality of Kpome (6°23′N, 2°13′E) (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between December 2013 and February 2014 (Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study presents new data from Kpome, distinguishing it from previous work in Pahou (Page 8).

supplement.evidence: While supplementary figures (S1, S2) are mentioned, the necessary genotype counts are provided in the main text on page 7.

assessment.summary: This study investigates insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus from Kpome, Benin, collected in 2013-2014. It reports high phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids, DDT, and bendiocarb. Molecular analysis of 92 field-collected mosquitoes revealed a high frequency of the GSTe2 L119F mutation (91% RR) and a very low frequency of the Rdl A296S mutation (1% RS). The study also examines the association between GSTe2 genotypes and DDT resistance phenotypes.
